commits.message: Add stable IDs and versioned state schemas

Add tui-execution boundary rule and meta-test

Forbid src/tui -> src/execution per ROADMAP Actor boundary. Meta-test cruises tmpdir fixtures via dependency-cruiser Node API to prove both forbidden rules fire, and asserts the real src/ cruise is non-vacuous (>15 modules, 0 violations) to prevent a TS7-style silent skip regression.

Fix pi-ai transitive type resolution for tsc

pi-ai 0.84.4's anthropic-messages.d.ts imports @anthropic-ai/sdk directly; the locked 0.91.1 types probe deep pnpm-style relative undici-types paths with same-line @ts-ignore comments, which cannot suppress TS2307 on the same line, breaking tsc under skipLibCheck: false on npm's flat layout. Override @anthropic-ai/sdk to 0.124.0 where upstream moved the ts-ignore onto its own line (default-export shape unchanged, compatible with pi-ai's usage). Also add devDependency @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.0 to satisfy the optional-peer type reference from @google/genai 1.52.0. No check configuration is changed.

Add PiRuntimeAdapter slice with fake-stream integration tests

PiRuntimeAdapter hides the pi-agent-core Agent behind private fields so hook fields stay frozen; terminal status is judged from the last assistant message's stopReason plus state.errorMessage, never the prompt() promise; Pi events are normalized into versioned EventEnvelopes (turn.started/completed, tool.proposed/settled, run.ended without success semantics); the injection snapshot is Value.Parse-validated and deep-frozen; interruption follows the fixed abort() then waitForIdle() posture; listener exceptions are swallowed and recorded instead of poisoning the run. Five scenarios cross the real Agent seam via a fake streamFn (prerecorded replies, deterministic chunk gate, controllable failure); verify gates all green (32 tests, deps 46 modules 0 violations).

Add dispose-before-run and idempotent dispose test

Cover two previously untested behavioral contracts: disposing an adapter that never ran must return promptly without throwing (upstream waitForIdle resolves immediately on an idle agent), and dispose must be idempotent while run() after dispose rejects. Also verify RunEndedPayload.messageCount semantics: the agent_end payload is the incremental newMessages (initialized at agent-loop.js:44, broadcast at lines 126/155/170), so the existing comment is accurate and stays unchanged.

commits.message:
Close phantom tool-name breaker blind spot at event level

Never-advertised tool names are intercepted by upstream prepareToolCall
(agent-loop.js:392-399) before beforeToolCall runs, so a model looping
on a phantom name spun forever: no hook, no ledger, no breaker.

Count consecutive phantom tool.settled events (isError and toolName not
in the advertised set) per tool name at the event layer; on reaching the
shared circuitBreakerThreshold, abort the run. Any non-phantom settled
event resets the streak. The hook-level breaker is untouched; the event
log (tool.proposed/tool.settled pairs) is the audit trail for the
phantom path, since no ToolExecution record can exist without the hook.

Replaces the stale KNOWN GAP comment with the closed design.

Persist rejection decisions to the ledger

Rejected calls previously left nothing on disk: intent is written only on
the allow path and Receipt v2 has no reason field, so the rejection reason
lived only in memory and evaporated on process exit.

Add a third ledger record family (decision) alongside intent and receipt,
persist it at all three rejection points in the approval gate (policy deny,
fail-closed without approval handler, human reject), and classify decision
lines as closed/rejected in cold-start reconcile -- never OutcomeUnknown.
A decision-write failure cannot change the already-blocked outcome; it is
routed to listenerErrors so the verbatim reason still reaches the model.
Close loop-breaker blind spots: upstream-intercepted, gate-exception, deny retry loops
Keep settled events logged and forwarded when receipt persistence fails
Assert deny reason reaches model-visible tool result in deny tests

commits.message: Add runtime event payload schemas as persistence single source
Add per-session event log writer with durability tiers and cold materializer
Reduce JsonlLedger to legacy reader and add one-shot migration into the event log
Cut adapter and CLI persistence over to the event log

Extend Receipt to v3 with content after-hash

M4 S2 hash auto-resolution groundwork: executed write receipts now carry
the measured post-write content hash (snapshotTag format) for cold-start
triangulation and torn-write detection. Assemble the receipt migration
chain (v1→v2→v3) once in state/receipt.ts and cut the legacy ledger
reader over to it.

Add breaker and resolution families to the event log

M4 S2 event log v2: intent records gain content hashes (before/expected-after)
for hash auto-resolution, tool.settled payloads gain the domain/environment
error kind, breaker trips and unknown-intent resolutions are persisted as
their own families. Reads route through the M0 migration pipeline
(event-log v1 to v2, embedded receipts v2 to v3); reconcile pairs
resolutions with dangling intents into a new resolved category.

Classify tool errors and add content-evidence probes

M4 S2 groundwork: classifyToolError sorts tool-thrown errors into domain
(business failure) vs environment (infrastructure) per D7; read_file domain
errors get a ReadFileError class so they are distinguishable from fs
exceptions. edit_file gains the ContentEvidenceTool capability: a zero
side-effect probe computing before/expected-after content hashes at
dispatch-preparation time and a post-execution target hash measurement.

Persist evidence hashes, error kinds, and breaker trips from the adapter

M4 S2 wiring: write-tier intents carry before/expected-after content hashes
from a zero side-effect tool probe (absent on probe failure, degrading to
human reconcile); executed receipts carry the measured post-write hash.
Tool execute wrappers capture the real thrown error and enrich tool.settled
with the D7 domain/environment error kind; upstream-intercepted errors
(validation failure, phantom tool names) are marked domain. Breaker trips
persist a breaker record with scope/count/threshold so cold classification
can tell governance aborts from user interrupts.

Add four-category failure classification to cold materialization and live runs

M4 S2 (D7): classifyRunOutcome/classifyToolOutcome are pure fact-based
functions shared by both surfaces. Run level: aborted without a breaker
record is a user cancel, with one a governance-breaker subclass; length is
business failure; syntheticFailure is infrastructure; everything else
falls to the unknown default bucket rather than a wrong label. Tool level:
aborted in-flight calls cancel (breaker-cut as subclass), domain errors
are business failures, environment exceptions infrastructure, unresolved
reconcile entries unknown. MaterializedSession exposes classification;
RunResult exposes the live failure class.

Auto-resolve dangling intents by content-hash triangulation at cold recovery

M4 S2 (D5 fold-in): recoverSession materializes a session, then for every
intent without a receipt reads the current file and compares three hashes -
match expected-after resolves executed, match before resolves not-executed
(the model may re-propose later; the system never re-executes), any
mismatch (torn write, third-party change, missing file) or missing intent
hashes stays OutcomeUnknown for a human. Each auto-resolution is persisted
as a resolution event-log record (fsync, idempotent per executionId) - no
silent bookkeeping. Crash-point matrix: before intent, between intent and
dispatch, after dispatch before receipt, mid-write.

Warn in the REPL when event persistence failures leave evidence gaps

M4 S2 (D2 visibility): when listenerErrors is non-empty the REPL prints an
explicit warning that N events failed to persist and the evidence chain is
incomplete - visible degradation, never pretending completeness. Checked at
startup (the future cold-resume path shares the same exit) and after every
run, delta-tracked to avoid re-printing unchanged failures.

Add session trace projection with id-verified linkage

M4 S3: buildSessionTrace projects a materialized session into a
turn-by-turn linked view - every tool call carries its proposed event,
intent/decision governance record, receipt, resolution, breaker trips
and failure classification. Links are keyed by (runId, toolCallId)
with executionId as the authoritative governance key; mismatched
toolCallIds, diverging args, or hash-evidence disagreement attach as
anomalies, and unpairable receipts/resolutions surface as orphans.
OutcomeUnknown intents are flagged pending-reconcile, never replayed.

Add read-only trace command rendering Chinese session reports

M4 S3: pigeon trace <sessionId> [--run <runId>] [--root <dir>] prints a
static one-shot report (D4) of the linked trace - approval provenance
per call (human / policy:yolo / policy:auto / policy:deny), verbatim
rejection reasons, hash evidence with expected-vs-observed verdicts,
failure badges in words (cancelled / breaker / business /
infrastructure / unknown), and inline pending-reconcile plus orphan
anomalies. Ids are short-hashed and oversized args truncated.
Read-only by construction: it only reads via materializeSession, never
opens an append handle, runs recovery, or touches the workspace.

Add read-only run replay projection with anomaly annotations
Extract shared CLI formatting helpers for report renderers
Add read-only replay command rendering raw run timelines
Wire replay subcommand into the CLI before model setup
Apply biome formatting to replay slice files

commits.message: Add session list projection
Add session list and resume commands
Add grant id kind, decision grant references, and dir containment check
Add grant event family, session grant store, and grants config

Surface grant approval sources and run context in approvals
Add session grant keys to the approval prompt

Add grants slash commands

Anchor config grant references to the promoted grant id and log promotions and removals

Config rule matches now reference promotedFrom.grantId instead of the array
index, so ledger references survive /revoke config#N reordering. /grants save
appends a grant.promoted record before writing the config and /revoke config#N
appends a grant.config-removed record after removing the rule; both are new
event log families (EVENT_LOG_VERSION 4 -> 5, additive). Promoting the same
grant twice is rejected so the grant id stays a unique identity.

Surface torn tails and entry sequence gaps in trace, replay and resume

materializeSession now derives entryGaps per run: holes between consecutive
runSeq values plus trailing entries implied by run.ended.messageCount. Trace
renders the torn tail and gaps under each run header and counts gaps in the
session header, replay annotates each hole in place and adds a trailing
summary, and resume lists torn tails, entry gaps and orphan records instead
of claiming the evidence chain is complete. Hand-written fixtures without
entries now report messageCount 0 so they stay consistent with the check.

Move schemas, materialization and projections into layered directories

Split persistence/event-log.ts into record schemas and the read-path
migration chain (state/event-log.ts), pure materialization with reconcile,
entry-gap detection and classification assembly (state/materialize.ts), the
JSONL storage engine (persistence/event-log.ts) and cold recovery
(execution/recovery.ts). Runtime event payload schemas move from pi-runtime
to state/runtime-events.ts so persistence no longer depends on the runtime.
Trace, replay, classification and the session summary become pure state
projections; grants split into schema (state), deterministic matching
(tools), the session grant store (approvals) and config file IO
(persistence). The adapter's event log sink is now a structural interface
over state input types, so pi-runtime never imports persistence.

dependency-cruiser gains six layering rules (state is a leaf; persistence and
tools depend only on state; approvals on state and tools; pi-runtime and
execution never reach storage or actor layers). Tests may cross layers to
build fixtures. No behaviour change: 265 tests unchanged.

Classify runs without run.ended as unknown and surface crash residue

A run whose event log lacks run.ended did not reach the end of the agent
loop, so the run-level classification now reports unknown regardless of
the last turn's stop reason; abort still emits agent_end upstream, so
cancelled runs are unaffected. Cold materialization exposes the list of
unfinished runs, resume lists them under the evidence gaps instead of
claiming the chain is complete, and the trace session header counts them
separately from write gaps. Found by the real-provider acceptance run.

Support thinking blocks in the fake stream fixture
Add a read-only streaming text observation port to the adapter
Move shared report wording into the application layer
Move the resume reconciliation flow into the application layer
Extract the assembly root into application/runtime.ts
Skeleton the tui layer and scope its upstream exemption to pi-tui

Move streamFn loading into the application assembly root

loadStreamFn is part of model wiring and belongs with buildRuntime;
cli and the upcoming tui entry both take it from application/, avoiding
an actor-to-actor import.

Add the M2 application shell with streaming message and input areas

pi-tui ProcessTerminal + TuiMainScreen minimal shell: message flow with
one Text per message (spike anti-pattern ban), streaming growth via
subscribeStream deltas, turn markers and tool call lines from runtime
events, user echo on submit, ASCII-only chrome. Input submission goes
only through the application API face; busy submissions are rejected
with the buffer kept (decision 027). Offscreen tests drive a Mock
Terminal + CJK-aware virtual screen and assert per-frame deltas, tool
lines, width invariants and dispose symmetry, plus a real-adapter
integration run.

Wire the tui entry point and export the shell surface

node src/tui/main.ts starts a ProcessTerminal-backed shell over the
shared application assembly root; approval handler is fail-closed until
the S3 approval panel lands (prompt always rejected with a verbatim
reason; the other five policy tiers are unaffected).

Move the grant command layer into application and share the path-arg extractor

The /grants command layer is Actor-shared logic: per decision 030 it lives
in application/ so the tui can project the same governance state without an
Actor-to-Actor dependency. extractPathArg moves to approvals/handler.ts as
the single convention for resolving the path argument of a call.

Extract the tui offscreen test harness into a shared fixture

The virtual screen emulator and mock terminal move to tui/testing.ts so the
S3 approval-panel and grants-view tests drive the shell through the same
offscreen path as the S2 shell tests.

Add the tui approval panel with the four-key verdict handler

The approval handler factory mirrors the cli semantics exactly: the promise
suspends on the panel, an input listener resolves [y/n/a/d], [a]/[d] create
session grants through the same store, and every cancel path fails closed
with a verbatim reason. While the panel holds, ordinary input is swallowed
(decision 029). The screen harness gains a left-margin strip in screenFlat
(pi-tui main-screen renders a one-cell margin) and a space-squash
normalizer for content-loss assertions, since word wrap eats spaces at
break points.

Wire slash commands into the tui shell for the grants view

/grants, /revoke and /grants save submit through the same application
command layer as the cli repl (decision 030); the write callback projects
output into the message flow. Slash submissions obey the busy rule like
any other input.

commits.message:
Wire the panel approval handler and grants context into the tui entry

main.ts replaces the fail-closed stopgap with the panel handler factory
(late-bound face over the shell) and passes the grants command context to
the shell.
Move the session list command layer into application
Add the session list and resume entries to the tui shell
Wire the session list and resume rebind factory into the tui entry
Move the failure badge wording into the shared actor format module
Add the cancel key and run terminal summary to the tui shell
Add the omp-style three-layer exit path to the tui shell

Move workspace preparation and grant seed restore into application

Both actor entries (cli/index.ts and tui/main.ts) carried their own copy of
the realpath normalisation, the legacy ledger migration and the restored
grant seed for resume. application/workspace.ts now owns prepareWorkspace,
restoreGrantSeed and sessionsDirOf, and a new dependency-cruiser rule keeps
actors away from the persistence write-side modules. The busy notice now
tells the user that a running session exits with Ctrl+C twice.

Make the TUI stream tail lazy so tool-only turns keep no placeholder child

MessageFlow.openStream now only resets streaming state on turn.started;
the tail Text is appended on the first text_delta, and closeStream adds
nothing for turns that never streamed. The invariant is literal: a tail
exists iff the turn produced text.

Empirical finding while re-checking M2 audit note-2: pi-tui 0.84.4
renders an empty Text as zero rows (early return in components/text.js,
padding included), so the always-open tail was never a visible blank
line. This change is invariant hygiene, not a visual
fix. The new shell test pins the observable contract (tool line flanked
by uniform spacing) and goes red if a placeholder tail ever becomes
visible or a library upgrade changes empty-Text semantics.

M2 audit note-3 (/grants duplicate lines) closed as not reproduced on a
real ConPTY terminal (scenario n3, zero model calls).
